correctness.rationale: Every extreme point for 1<s<2 is a signed two-support vector (1,s-1,0,...); the dual support norm is the top-two weighted sum. The incident facet normals at one vertex are explicit. All dual pair distances give (1+(s-1)^2)/s in dimension two, 2/s in dimension three, and 2 in higher dimensions, with separate endpoint witnesses. Complete quantified proof and 20 reproducible finite exact-rational replays support, but the latter are not a general proof.

value.rationale: The family is a canonical continuous interpolation between two fundamental Banach balls, previously studied for geometry and optimization. The exact sharp coefficient classifies approximate smoothness for every dimension and parameter and uncovers a rigid dimension-four obstruction plus discontinuous endpoint collapse. This supplies a natural previously untabulated invariant, not an arbitrary isolated rational example.
